To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CH molecule correlates tightly with E(BV) and with H_2 column density while the CN molecule does not show such correlation.
the CH and CH+ column densities are well correlated with interstellar extinction, while the CN is not.

CH and CH+ column densities correlate well with E(B-V), the correlation of CH with E(B-V)/N(H_2) is even tighter, the relation between CN and E(B-V) is less obvious, the correlation of CN with E(B-V)/(N(H_2)*N(C+)) is tight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical composition of the interstellar matter in relation to interstellar extinction.
the relation between interstellar extinction and abundancies of CH, CH+, and CN.
the problem of the origin of interstellar extinction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CH molecule is the only one of the studied molecules which is well spatially correlated with dust.
the CH molecule is a good tracer of interstellar dust while the CN molecule is not.
CN is a good tracer of the gas phase chemistry while the CH and CH+ molecule are good tracers of the grain surface chemistry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CH and CH cations are the best tracers of dust in translucent clouds while CN is not.
CH and CH cations are good tracers of interstellar extinction and they can be used to derive E(B-V) values for the lines of sight which are not covered by photometric measurements.
CH, CH+ are formed in the gas phase and are spatially correlated to the dust, while the CN is formed in the gas and is not spatially correlated to dust.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CH molecule may serve as a tracer of interstellar extinction in the near-infrared spectral range.
the CH molecule is the most reliable probe of the total column of interstellar matter.
CH and CH+, as well as CN, can be used as tracers of dust.
